item.title: The Recursive Dollhouse: The Recursive Dollhouse
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Fridge Horror/Emotional

Elevator Pitch: Essentially, SCP-XXXX a dollhouse of whatever environment it is currently being contained within. Likewise, it would sustain a diminished capability of whatever building it is housed in. SCP-XXXX-1 are essentially "dolls" housed in the facility that make up sentient/concious organisms. This also applies to anomalous materials as well, such as me, the toaster that speaks in the first person or the mask SCP. In addition, the anomalous effects of objects are still maintained but to a much smaller degree. Objects within the SCP-XXXX move in tandem with their current reality counterparts. Actions made within the main facility are mirrored in SCP-XXXX. There is in fact a miniature version of SCP-XXXX (dubbed SCP-XXXXa) and it is theorized that there are multiple versions of SCP-XXXX that exist within the dimensional realm.

Central Narrative: The SCP Foundation found this dollhouse in the middle of a nursery amongst other toys. After examining this, an entity attempts to contact them (potentially, though I am not sold on the concept) in an attempt to get it back.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The inherent dread of a recursive universe where what we view from within could in fact be caused by an upper plane of existence is terrifying, no?

Additional Notes: Edit 1: As for what happens when objects or instances of SCP-XXXX-1 are affected by outside users, I'd like to go into that further within test logs potentially. If not, essentially, the-what I dub-"dollhouse reality" can be affected by users. The current reality would be marginally affected in a similar manner. This isn't compulsory, however, but it does bring about satisfaction of the affected individual to complete said task. Other more violent actions such as the destruction of an instance of SCP-XXXX-1 can cause a severely minimized effect on the affected individual.If an anomalous SCP-XXXX-1 instance comes in contact with a non-anomalous instance of SCP-XXXX-1, the effects that would be generated by the anomalous instance are greatly minimized. Objects brought into the SCP-XXXX reality will manifest in the current reality as well.

item.title: (Seeking Greenlight) 'In Your Dreams: An instructional video on how to get the best sleep possible': (Seeking Greenlight) 'In Your Dreams: An instructional video on how to get the best sleep possible'
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Psychological Horror

Page Layout (Optional): More or less a traditional SCP article, though I plan to include a transcript of the tape and test results of those who viewed the tape.

Elevator Pitch: This SCP takes the form of a video tape. It is labelled 'In Your Dreams: an instructional video on how to get the best sleep possible' It starts out as a sleep instructional video before descending into madness, including subliminal messaging. The contents of the tape lead to massive psychological effects on whoever views the whole thing.

Central Narrative: The tape was discovered in the home of a suicide victim. The individual had no psychological issues prior to the viewing of the tape, which caught the attention of the SCP foundation. Attempts to find any info on the tape's origin has proven unsuccessful. However, the foundation has discovered multiple cases of homicides and suicides linked to this tape. All of the people who have viewed the tape and comply with all of its instructions suffer from insomnia, delusions, prone to self harm, sociopathic tendencies, and decreased empathy/compassion. Some extreme cases include incoherent rambling, and repeating the phrase "THERE ARE NO FACES."

In one incident, a copy of the tape was reportedly aired on TV in Mason County, Washington. Those who viewed the tape have received Class A amnesiacs, which have been proven successful with reversing the tapes effects

Hook/Attention-Grabber: There will be a disclaimer on the top stating that any staff who view the tape will be subject to Class A amnesiacs and an emergency psychological evaluation and that any unauthorized viewing of the tape will lead to termination, and any attempts at distributing the tape will lead to termination or reassignment to D-class.

Additional Notes: This was inspired by Local58's "real sleep". Honestly, the whole series is SCP material.

item.title: SCP Idea: The Muse: SCP Idea: The Muse
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Psychological Horror

Page Layout (Optional): Standard + Exploration logs

Elevator Pitch: From the perspective of the affected, a voice calls to them from inside their head, claiming to be their subconscious. It helps them along, allows them to remember things better, formulate ideas faster, etc. After a while, it will take the form of a humanoid hallucination, engaging in long conversations with the victim. The victim becomes more and more detached from reality, spiraling into ritual and insanity as the "muse" takes over more and more of their mind, eventually taking full control of their body.

Central Narrative: A small foundation site collapses as the head researcher comes under the affect of the Muse.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The reveal of the muse not being a figment of the victim's mind but rather an independent entity.

Additional Notes: I think this could either turn out very good and interesting or very cliché.

item.title: Parasitic Amoeba: Parasitic Amoeba
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX Is a species of omnivorous amoeba that travel extremely fast throughout liquids and can terminate any organism in seconds.

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX-1 usually appears to those who have a small paycheck and have ease of access to a large container for water. Then SCP-XXXX-1 will dump a colony of SCP-XXXX into said container when the owner is near it. After dumping the colony the owner of the container will be frozen in place while SCP-XXXX walks towards and eventually into them, tell them to take care of the colony and then de-manifest.

Attention Grabber: I feel like there are a lot of SCPs that are either monstrous, cute or funny. But not all SCPs have to be that way. Another thing is that one thing goes through my head every time I hear of a K-Class end of the world scenario, that the world can be ended by something as big as a meteor or something as small as a micro-organism. I feel like there aren't enough small organisms in foundation custody that are capable of causing such an event.

item.title: SCP Idea "Thunder": Re: SCP Idea "Thunder"
item.content:encoded:
This is one of those weird ones: It's a great idea, but it's more of a cute one than anything else. You're going to need to show that the dog actually has an effect on its environment for it to be taken seriously; basically, you need to show that the dog is real despite being invisible.

I would, however, suggest you forego the vet report. To really have fun with SCP you need to do an interesting balancing act: You need to create doubt that the dog exists even as you need to show that it exists. This means that you need to show that the dog exists while at the same foregoing forensic evidence that it exists. So responding to barking before someone knocks on the door is cool, but a vet report not so much. Showing that a pair of slippers has been retrieved without him getting up is cool, but having film that the slippers are floating through the air not so much.

If you can hit that balance and create that doubt while not dispelling it either way you should be able to create a great SCP.

item.title: (Seeking Greenlight) The Abnormal High School: (Seeking Greenlight) The Abnormal High School
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Action

Elevator Pitch: twenty-five (25) humanoids, thirteen (13) male humanoids, and twelve (12) female humanoids that're infected by an unknown phenomenon in an abandoned high school that turns them into mutants with dangerous abilities.

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX, also known as "The Abnormal High School," is a high-school located somewhere deep in the woods, abandoned due to the place where it was being built was used as a testing zone for nuclear weapons of the government. In the year 2006, twenty-five individuals who are runaways had entered the school as they experienced a mysterious headache that causes them to faint for a long time after they were awake; they've discovered that they're not normal anymore, or to be specific; they have become something that cannot be explained. SCP-XXXX was brought to the Foundation's attention when they've received witness reports of a boy levitating in the middle of the air, at the same time altering the wind, as they've discovered that the humanoid male is located in an area with nuclear waste. This resulted in dispatching as Task-Force MTF Beta-7 as they were a success in retrieving all of the subjects that're in SCP-XXXX

+ show block
– hide block

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The origins of SCP-XXXX trace back to the early 19s. A mysterious asteroid landed into the abandoned high-school after it was tested by the government's nuclear weapons, which the school was completely obliterated into oblivion. However, with the asteroid's presence, it has been reconstructed back as new.

Additional Notes: Hope you enjoy it.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: The electric dog: The electric dog
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page type: SCP Article

Elevator pitch: The SCP is a dog that can summon and redirect lighting. Most of the time it looks and acts like a normal dog except a tear in it's flesh on it's left shoulder blade.

Central narrative: SCP-XXXX draws electricity into it's body so no open electrical devices can be near it. When electricity enters it's body, it turns hostile and attacks anything near it. It stays like this for around 10-30 minutes depending on the amount of electricity that entered it's body.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It was found near a power plant in England after the police reported a dog "throwing lightning at them".

item.title: A helping hand (Seeking Greenlight): A helping hand (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: This SCP involves a floating hand which assists people with things when they are needed, the SCP teleports to anyone who says they need help with something, this will not work if they are only thinking of needing help and not saying it,

Central Narrative: The hand is cut off at the wrist area, the inside shows a black void.
Testing showed that it can only help with things if it's within a 5 meter radius and will help with anything it can, it can hammer a nail in the wall, or shoot a target as long as it's within 5 meters of the person needing help.

It is able to teleport anywhere on the world and wont stay any longer than needed so containment isn't possible and has since been classified as Keter, it's presence was noticed by the foundation in 2011 when a twitter user Robert Hexain posted a message about the SCP who helped him repair his roof.

When there are multiple people in need of assistance it will randomly choose one to help and will help the other later if they still need help, during testing a tracker was put on the SCP to locate it at all times to see who the SCP helped, they will then be tracked down, interviewed and given Class B amnestics

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It can be helpful or it can be really dangerous

item.title: Two Dimensional Love: Re: Two Dimensional Love
item.content:encoded:
But I really like the cultural appropriation idea, what if instead of a lonely Japanese man it's a Western otaku who ends up being killed by it due to messing with things he doesn't truly understand?

How would this explore the cultural appropriation idea? It also feels like you'd still be keeping a lot of the more…shock orientated aspects of this in and I'm not really sure I vibe with them.

I guess at the end of the day, the tl;dr of what I am saying here is: just passively showing these events happen is likely gonna be pretty underwhelming, and a lot of how well this works will be dependent on like…the framing and the characterisation and what you say with them.

I'm also really not sure about the continued focus on pre-containment stuff: a SCP article is written from the perspective of the Foundation and so you generally need them to be actively involved in the story, usually in a literary protagonistic way, y'know

item.title: SCP Idea (Seeking Greenlight): Elaine of Astolat's Curse: Re: SCP Idea (Seeking Greenlight): Elaine of Astolat's Curse
item.content:encoded:
This feels somewhat reminiscent of SCP-4205 in the way that the people affected by the anomaly react and like, what happens to them; and I'm not exactly sure how this ties into Elaine of Astolat.

Really my biggest concern with this, narratively speaking, is it feels very passive: there's not really any kind of narrative stakes or anything pulling the story forward; so it ends up feeling very flat. It feels like there really needs to be more of an indication of how the increase in -1 occurrences is causing the Foundation to more and more desperately look into this.

It also feels very flat: there's not a lot of growth or change between the start of the story and the end, and the only real difference I can see is that everyone knows more about what is going. It really feels like it needs something permanent to happen here: for the SCP to understand what is happening and change as a result, or for the Foundation to find stuff out and react by changing containment procedures or doing new experiments or something.

item.title: The No-Tell Motel: Re: The No-Tell Motel
item.content:encoded:
Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror, (Some) Comedy, Sci-Fi

Page Layout (Optional): Article Format

Elevator Pitch:

⦁ A seemingly unassuming small hotel in the Mojave Desert

⦁ The interior is infinitely larger than the exterior

⦁ The motel is a fixed point in multiple realities

⦁ There's no observable staff from outside, but inside there is

⦁ Those who have seen the staff cannot recall any physical features, only that they are polite and courteous

⦁ Some staff have personalities that can be recalled, but that is the only memorable trait they have

⦁ Those who stay past check out are escorted out by security, also whose features are unable to be recalled

⦁ Occasionally, those that check in are altered to have an anomalous ability/property, and it is hinted by the staff that that's one of the reasons why they are drawn in

⦁ The halls are infinite and labyrinthine

⦁ The motel rooms are generic and normal-seeming

⦁ The motel room windows each look out on different worlds

⦁ Some people who leave the motel are from alternate Earths

⦁ Despite the monitoring and security, somehow, sometimes some people manage to get past to check in

⦁ An exploration log will be included, detailing science teams with armed escorts as well as D-class personnel teams exploring the Motel's interior

⦁ A breach log which will detail instances where civilians attempt to gain entry to the site, have gained entry, as well as those who managed to make it into the motel. This log will also include instances where those who entered are recovered. It will also detail instances where on-site personnel themselves attempted to check in to the motel.

Central Narrative: World-building

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The motel occasionally has a guest who stays in a room that looks out onto our world, and the dressers are filled with money from different time periods and countries, some of which no longer exist or have never existed. And the money includes ancient drachmas, crudely carved red painted stones, and etc.

Additional Notes: I'm not sure where I need help, but I gladly accept any advice willing to be given!
